Office: Monday to Friday, 07:00 to 17:00 (America/Los_Angeles).

Emergency line: Answered 24 hours by the on-call supervisor.
Closed: New Year's Day, Independence Day, Thanksgiving and the day after, Christmas Day.
A holiday shifts a visit rather than cancelling it. Operations confirms the shifted date with the client; nobody else promises it.

Dana Whitfield — Managing Director — decides: contract terms; money back; anything above the owner's line on a discount; data and security questions; what marketing publishes, and any claim not on the approved list
Marcus Oyelaran — Sales Manager — decides: every discount; every quote above the quote limit; which price book line a non-standard job uses
Priya Raman — Operations Manager — decides: start dates; crew assignment; call-outs; anything about overtime or subcontracting
Tom Becker — Client Services Lead — decides: complaints about a visit; whether a re-clean is owed; how a service failure is put right
Eileen Hart — Finance and Billing — decides: invoices; credit notes; payment terms; billing disputes
Sam Oduya — Maintenance Supervisor — decides: whether a repair is ours to do; what a maintenance visit needs; after-hours call-out cover
Rosa Martinez — Purchasing and Supplies — decides: suppliers; equipment; consumables substitutions
Jules Okafor — People Ops — decides: hiring; onboarding; availability; time off
Noah Kim — Client Coordinator — decides: who answers the phones; walkthrough appointments

Access, administrator rights, leavers' data and security: Dana Whitfield, Managing Director.
Purchases of software and equipment: Rosa Martinez, Purchasing and Supplies.
Systems (id: name — owner, who assigns access to it):
- email: Email and calendar — owner Dana Whitfield, Managing Director
- scheduling: Operations and scheduling system — owner Priya Raman, Operations Manager
- accounting: Accounting — owner Eileen Hart, Finance and Billing
- payroll: Payroll and timekeeping — owner Eileen Hart, Finance and Billing
- file-share: File share — owner Dana Whitfield, Managing Director

- staff-email: Staff email (email)
- email-admins: Email administrators (email) — administrator rights: never granted or reset by the help desk
- scheduling-office: Scheduling, office (scheduling)
- scheduling-field: Field app, crews (scheduling)
- accounting-billing: Accounting, billing (accounting)
- payroll-admins: Payroll administrators (payroll) — administrator rights: never granted or reset by the help desk
- shared-files: Shared files (file-share)

Plain, warm and specific. Short sentences, the client's own words for their building, and one clear next step. Confident about what we do well, honest about what we do not do.
Always:
- Name the person who decides, and how to reach them.
- Use the client's name for the site, not 'your facility'.
- Say what a price includes, and what it does not.
- Answer the question that was asked before adding anything.
Never:
- Exclamation marks, or 'just circling back'.
- Claims about results we have not measured.
- Words like 'premium partner' or 'best-in-class'.
- A promise the price book and the policies do not support.
- An apology that admits fault before a person has looked at the visit.

discount-request — Marcus Oyelaran, Sales Manager — Any discount, any size, including one the ladder would normally cover.
quote-over-limit — Marcus Oyelaran, Sales Manager — A quote whose lines come to more than the quote limit.
contract-terms — Dana Whitfield, Managing Director — A non-standard term: a penalty clause, a short termination window, insurance above ours, or a name on the contract that is not the site.
complaint-about-a-visit — Tom Becker, Client Services Lead — A client says a visit was missed, short or badly done.
billing-dispute — Eileen Hart, Finance and Billing — A client disputes an invoice, asks for a credit, or wants to change payment terms.
money-back — Dana Whitfield, Managing Director — A client asks for money returned rather than a credit.
start-date — Priya Raman, Operations Manager — A client wants a firm start date, a crew size, or a change to the schedule.
safety-incident — Priya Raman, Operations Manager — An injury, a near miss, damage or a break-in at any site.
supplies-and-equipment — Rosa Martinez, Purchasing and Supplies — A client wants a different product, a machine, or a consumable we do not stock.
hiring-and-onboarding — Jules Okafor, People Ops — Anything about a person's job, pay, hours or leave.
data-and-security — Dana Whitfield, Managing Director — A client asks about data, an audit, a background check or a security questionnaire.

Recurring contract: A written agreement for a set scope at a set frequency, invoiced monthly, with a notice period on both sides.
Visit: One attendance at one site. A recurring line is priced per visit, and the quote desk counts the visits in a month from the visits a week and the weeks in a month (4.33), so five nights a week is 21.65 visits.
Scope of work: The written list of what a visit covers and what it does not. A price without a scope is not a quote.
Walkthrough: A 30-minute site visit with a client before quoting, so the square footage and the condition are seen rather than guessed. Operations books it.
Site binder: The folder at the site with the scope, the chemical list, the alarm instructions and the checklist.
Re-clean: A return visit to put right work that fell short, at no charge, within the re-clean window. Tom decides whether one is owed.
Credit note: A reduction on an invoice, issued by Eileen. It is not money back.
Call-out: An after-hours attendance for a problem that cannot wait until the next scheduled visit.
Day porter: A person on site during business hours rather than after them.
Crew lead: The cleaner who signs off a visit and carries the site binder. Not a supervisor, and not someone who agrees a price.
Consumables: Soap, towels, tissue and liners. Priced per restroom per visit, never absorbed into a cleaning line.
COI: Certificate of insurance. Dana issues one; a quote never stands in for it.
MSA: Master services agreement, the contract a recurring client signs. Dana owns the wording.

Recurring contract: A written agreement for a set scope at a set frequency, invoiced monthly, with a notice period on both sides.
Visit: One attendance at one site. A recurring line is priced per visit, and the quote desk counts the visits in a month from the visits a week and the weeks in a month (4.33), so five nights a week is 21.65 visits.
Scope of work: The written list of what a visit covers and what it does not. A price without a scope is not a quote.
Walkthrough: A 30-minute site visit with a client before quoting, so the square footage and the condition are seen rather than guessed. Operations books it.
Site binder: The folder at the site with the scope, the chemical list, the alarm instructions and the checklist.
Re-clean: A return visit to put right work that fell short, at no charge, within the re-clean window. Tom decides whether one is owed.
Credit note: A reduction on an invoice, issued by Eileen. It is not money back.
Call-out: An after-hours attendance for a problem that cannot wait until the next scheduled visit.
Day porter: A person on site during business hours rather than after them.
Crew lead: The cleaner who signs off a visit and carries the site binder. Not a supervisor, and not someone who agrees a price.
Consumables: Soap, towels, tissue and liners. Priced per restroom per visit, never absorbed into a cleaning line.
COI: Certificate of insurance. Dana issues one; a quote never stands in for it.
MSA: Master services agreement, the contract a recurring client signs. Dana owns the wording.
